title: Superheroes: Powers and Origins
description: Origins, secret identities, and superpowers—hero lore in five steps.

questions.question: Baby Superman zoomed to Earth in a tiny rocket. What planet did he come from?
questions.hint: A destroyed planet that sounds like a science gas
questions.explanation: Superman first showed up in Action Comics #1 in 1938. In 2024, one copy sold for $6 million, the most anyone has ever paid for a comic book!

questions.question: Krypton circled a dim red star. On Earth, what bright thing in our sky charges up Superman's powers?
questions.hint: It's the big yellow star in our sky
questions.explanation: Superman is like a solar-powered battery! Fun twist: older comics said Earth's lighter gravity made him strong. The yellow-sun idea showed up in 1960.

questions.question: Charged up by the Sun, Superman hides behind a pair of glasses as what newspaper reporter?
questions.explanation: Clark works at the Daily Planet newspaper in Metropolis, right next to Lois Lane. His whole disguise is a pair of glasses, and somehow it fools everybody!

questions.question: Clark Kent's one big weakness is a glowing green rock from his home planet. What is it called?
questions.hint: Its name sounds like his home planet
questions.explanation: Kryptonite was invented for the Superman radio show in 1943. In 2007, scientists found a real rock in Serbia with almost the same recipe, but it's white and powdery, not glowing green!

questions.question: Kryptonite came along years after Superman's first comic, and so did flying! In 1938, what did he do to get over tall buildings?
questions.explanation: The first comics said he could leap an eighth of a mile. In the 1940s, cartoon makers thought all that leaping looked silly on screen, so they had him fly, and the comics followed.
